title: Reduce KV mmap fragmentation and introduce cooperative batcher yield
creator: Maya Patel
description: Symptoms: production nodes report increasing resident set size and sporadic OOM kills under long-lived inference workloads with many different model shards. Investigation shows heavy mmap fragmentation in the KV cache arena and long-running batcher lanes that monopolize CPU while waiting for IO/kvcache priming. Goal: reduce mmap fragmentation and peak RSS by implementing an arena compaction/munmap/madvise strategy for cold KV pages, and add a cooperative yield mechanism in the continuous batcher so lanes that are waiting (e.g., for kvcache fetches or remote fetch) will yield control to other lanes to lower tail latency and improve throughput packing.
background: We already have several related refactors (slot prewarmer, batch windowing, lease reclaimer). However, VMs with high churn in keys slowly accumulate non-contiguous mmapped regions from the KV page allocator. Combined with spinner-heavy batcher lanes, this leads to elevated tail latencies and occasional crashes in memory-constrained environments (notably Dedicated small GPU pools). Previous attempts at aggressive GC caused latency spikes. This ticket aims for a minimal-safe approach: incremental, observable compaction and a low-overhead yield path for the batcher.
non_goals: This work will not change the high-level cache eviction policy (LRU tiers) nor introduce a new on-disk store format. We will not migrate to a different allocator in this ticket. Long-term memory allocator replacement is a separate initiative.
tech_decisions: Use madvise(MADV_DONTNEED) + background worker for page reclamation rather than immediate munmap to avoid breaking address space assumptions during GC.

Implement a cooperative yield hook in the continuous batcher: lanes check yield conditions before heavy spinning and call a lightweight scheduler_yield() that uses futex/condition-variable wait with short timeouts when appropriate.
Expose kvcache page hotness metric (kvcache.page_hotness_bucket) to decide safe candidates for compaction.
Prefer conservative thresholds by default (compaction only when RSS > configured high watermark for > 5m) and surface as config flags to Dedicated/Private customers.
Instrument and gate changes behind runtime flags (--kv-compact-enabled, --batcher-cooperative-yield) so we can roll back quickly if regressions occur.
Add unit + integration tests that simulate fragmentation patterns using our memory-fuzz harness; add perf benchmark that measures tail P95/P99 token latency under synthetic key-churn workload.
Avoid language-level GC interactions: keep compaction worker in separate process threadpool to reduce pause coupling.
Plan for compatibility with present KVCACHE checksum/serialization format; no on-disk format changes.
Key trade-off: madvise trades potential page faults on reuse for lower RSS; chosen because it is reversible and less invasive than munmap.

Cooperative yield trade-offs: slight overhead on fast paths due to additional condition checks vs large win in reduced blocking; will benchmark to choose frequency of checks (e.g., every N iterations or after X microseconds).
acceptance_criteria: Unit and integration tests covering compaction worker and batcher yield pass in CI.
Production-like perf job (kvmem-churn benchmark) shows >= 25% reduction in peak RSS and >= 10% improvement in P99 latency under the same QPS compared to baseline.
No increase in error rates or client-visible 5xxs in staged canary for 48 hours at 20% traffic during rollout.
Runtime flags successfully disable behavior and rollback plan documented in PR description.
Observability: new metrics for kv_compaction_runs_total, kv_compaction_pages_reclaimed, batcher_yield_count, and a dashboard update are created and linked.
Design doc reviewed and approved by runtime performance and infra leads (Riya Singh, Tomas Kline).
